cases.customer_question: How should HCI test-mode readiness be verified before Bluetooth RF qualification testing?
question_variants: How do we confirm the product is ready for RF testing?
Why does HCI Reset fail during test setup?
How can we validate HCI mode operation before qualification testing?
What should be checked when HCI commands do not execute?
How do we confirm test-mode communication is working?
cases.actual_issue: Establishing reliable HCI communication and test-mode operation before formal Bluetooth RF qualification testing begins.
cases.plain_english_explanation: RF qualification testing requires the device to enter the correct Bluetooth test mode and respond to HCI commands. Early setup problems can appear as communication or serial-port errors. Verifying HCI operation before scheduling formal testing reduces qualification delays.
cases.consultant_answer: The parties worked through HCI-mode setup verification, investigated HCI Reset command failures, confirmed command execution, and ultimately validated that the development platform could be switched into HCI mode correctly. Test-mode operation was treated as completed before proceeding with qualification activities.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth RF qualification depends on reliable access to the controller through HCI test mechanisms. Test readiness must be confirmed before formal RF measurements are scheduled.
cases.final_recommendation: Verify HCI-mode configuration, command transport, and successful HCI command execution before beginning RF qualification testing. Resolve communication errors during setup validation rather than during formal testing.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Failure to validate HCI communication can delay RF testing, create troubleshooting cycles during scheduled test time, and postpone qualification completion.
